description: Server conformance transcript of file transfer v2 (the parts protocol, docs/FILES_V2_PARTS_PROTOCOL.md). Generated by running the scenarios against the real handlers of internal/filesv2; every client replays the same scenarios against its fake and compares status, error code and the selected headers and JSON fields. Format: docs/FILES_V2_SERVER_TRANSCRIPT.md.

constants.clock: every scenario starts its fake clock at clock_start_ms and moves it only with advance_clock; the cleanup runs only with the cleanup step (the real worker runs hourly)

error_codes_not_in_the_transcript.files_unavailable: 503 with Retry-After 60, answered by the glue of cmd/bcrypto-lite when files.db could not be opened at boot (tested there)

scenario_requirement_tags.concurrency: needs requests in flight at the same time (async, stall, release, await)
scenario_requirement_tags.large_declared: declares objects of up to MAX_BLOB; no byte of them is ever sent, a fake must not allocate them
scenario_requirement_tags.linux_statfs: the real server can only reproduce it where the free space of the volume can be read (Linux)
scenario_requirement_tags.raw_request: sends bodies, paths or methods that no client of the protocol produces (malformed JSON, unknown routes); a fake that is not an HTTP server can skip them
scenario_requirement_tags.raw_tcp_half_close: needs a raw TCP connection that half-closes after a short body: the only way a client reads the short_body answer, an ordinary HTTP stack reports its own connection error instead
scenario_requirement_tags.real_time_wait: waits for a server timer in real time (up to 5 seconds)
scenario_requirement_tags.server_seam: drives a server-internal condition (the create gate, the download slots, the disk floor) that a fake models as a switch

pattern.name: fmix32
pattern.spec: byte(i) = fmix32(u32(i) XOR u32(seed * 0x9E3779B9)) AND 0xFF, where u32 takes the low 32 bits, the multiplication is mod 2^32 and fmix32 is the MurmurHash3 32-bit finalizer (h ^= h >> 16; h *= 0x85EBCA6B; h ^= h >> 13; h *= 0xC2B2AE35; h ^= h >> 16, all mod 2^32). i is the absolute index in the blob, 0 for the first byte of the header.

scenarios.name: create_success_and_header_region
scenarios.description: A first create answers 201 with Location and the geometry of the object. The 64-byte header exists from that moment: it can be read before any part has been sent. The parts map starts empty.

scenarios.name: create_is_idempotent_on_the_header
scenarios.description: A second create by the same account with the same 64 bytes and the same length returns the existing object (200, existing:true) with the parts already received; existing, received and complete are left out when false or zero. Asking for a token on the repeat gives a fresh token. Another account with the same header gets an object of its own.

scenarios.name: create_after_delete_makes_a_new_object
scenarios.description: Deleting an object frees its header: the same create afterwards is a 201 with a new object id, and the old id is gone.

scenarios.name: create_head_conflict
scenarios.description: The same 64-byte header with another length is a conflict, not a silent reuse (409 head_conflict). The check comes before the account's limits. Deleting the first object frees the header for the other length.

scenarios.name: create_validation_errors
scenarios.description: Every way a create body can be wrong, in the order the server checks: body shape (bad_request), blob_len (bad_blob_len, blob_too_large), part_size, head, then the token request. Nothing is reserved by a refused create.

scenarios.name: create_and_token_need_the_files_entitlement
scenarios.description: Creating an object and issuing a token need feat.files (402 entitlement_required with feature and package). Transferring parts, completing, reading, deleting and the collection routes do not: an account that lost the entitlement can still finish and free what it holds.

steps.note: the entitlement is checked before the repeat is recognised

scenarios.name: quota_default_is_one_maximum_object
scenarios.description: With the default quota (MAX_BLOB) one maximum-size object fills an account: the next create, however small, is 413 quota_exceeded with used and limit. Another account is not affected, and a delete frees the room at once. The object is declared only: no byte of it is ever sent.

scenarios.name: quota_counts_every_object_until_it_is_deleted
scenarios.description: The per-account quota sums the declared size of EVERY object the account still has: finished or not, idle or not. Completing an object frees nothing; neither does waiting. Only a delete (or the cleanup) does, at once.

steps.note: a completed object still counts
idle time frees nothing
another account has its own quota
the delete freed the room at once

scenarios.name: too_many_objects
scenarios.description: An account may have at most MaxObjectsPerUser live objects, whatever their size or state (429 too_many_objects, no Retry-After). Completing one does not free a row; deleting does.

scenarios.name: too_many_uploads_idle_ones_count
scenarios.description: An account may have 10 unfinished objects (429 too_many_uploads with limit and Retry-After 30). Idle ones count: waiting frees no slot. A repeat of an existing create (a resume) is never refused by a cap; completing an object frees its slot; another account is not affected.

steps.note: idle objects still hold their slot
a resume needs no room and is never refused by a cap
the completion freed a slot

scenarios.name: create_limits_objects_before_uploads
scenarios.description: When several limits are exceeded at once the object count is reported first, then the unfinished count, then the quota.

steps.note: a completed object still holds a row

scenarios.name: create_limits_uploads_before_quota
scenarios.description: The unfinished-object cap is reported before the quota; a repeat with another length is a head_conflict before either; the quota answer names what the account uses.

scenarios.name: create_and_token_requests_with_malformed_bodies
scenarios.description: A request body that is not the JSON object the route takes (cut off, empty, followed by more data, not JSON at all) is 400 bad_request, and nothing is created. These are bodies no client of the protocol sends; a fake that is not an HTTP server can skip the scenario.

steps.note: data after the JSON object

scenarios.name: server_wide_cap_on_unfinished_bytes
scenarios.description: All accounts together may hold only so many declared bytes in unfinished objects (here 3000): a create over it is 507 insufficient_storage with Retry-After 60. The account's own limits are reported first, a resume is never refused, idle time frees nothing, and completing, deleting or the cleanup do.

steps.note: the account's own limits are reported first
a resume is never refused by the server-wide cap
idle time frees nothing
a completed object no longer counts
the cleanup removed the idle objects of carol, dave and eve

scenarios.name: server_wide_cap_default_is_16_gib
scenarios.description: With the default cap of 16 GiB of declared unfinished bytes, three maximum-size objects of three accounts fit and a fourth is 507 insufficient_storage with Retry-After 60. The objects are declared only.

scenarios.name: insufficient_storage_when_the_disk_floor_is_reached
scenarios.description: When the volume would have less than the free-space floor left after the object (or the preallocation reports no space), the create is 507 insufficient_storage WITHOUT Retry-After (a full disk does not clear in a minute) and nothing is left behind.

scenarios.name: create_busy_when_the_disk_turn_is_taken
scenarios.description: Creates that touch the disk take turns. One that waits longer than CreateGateWait for its turn is 429 create_busy with Retry-After 2 and takes nothing; the one holding the turn finishes normally and the retry succeeds.

scenarios.name: part_upload_in_any_order_and_parts_map
scenarios.description: Parts may arrive in any order. Each answer carries the part, whether it was a duplicate, how many parts are on disk and how many there are. GET parts returns the bitmap: bit i mod 8 of byte i div 8, least significant bit first, set when part i is on disk.

scenarios.name: parts_map_bit_order_across_bytes
scenarios.description: The bitmap is least significant bit first and spans bytes in order: with 10 parts, part 1 is bit 1 of byte 0 (0x02) and part 9 is bit 1 of byte 1 (0x02). complete with parts missing lists the first missing indices.

scenarios.name: part_duplicate_same_digest_and_conflict
scenarios.description: The same part with the same digest is a success (duplicate:true), even when the body that comes with it is not the part: the body is read and discarded and a part on disk never changes. A different digest is 409 part_conflict, decided before a byte is written.

steps.note: a corrupt body under the known digest is still a duplicate
the stored part is still the first one
another digest: refused, nothing written

scenarios.name: part_digest_mismatch_is_not_marked
scenarios.description: A body that does not match its Content-Digest is 400 digest_mismatch and the part is NOT marked: the parts map and the received count do not change. The retry with the right bytes goes through and overwrites the bad region.

steps.note: one bit flipped in transit; the digest is of the real part
the owner reads a part of an unfinished object

scenarios.name: part_content_digest_header_rules
scenarios.description: Content-Digest (RFC 9530) must carry a sha-256 member that is a byte sequence of 32 bytes: missing or only another algorithm is digest_required, anything malformed (or the sha-256 member twice) is digest_invalid; both answer with Want-Content-Digest. Other algorithms in the same header are ignored.

steps.note: none of the refused uploads marked the part

scenarios.name: part_length_and_index_rules
scenarios.description: The body length must be exactly the part's (bad_length, with the expected length), and known (chunked is 411 length_required). The part index must be a canonical integer below the part count (bad_part), checked before the object is looked up; the owner is checked before the range. The length is checked before the digest.

steps.note: the length is checked before the digest
the index is checked before the object is looked up
the owner is checked before the range

scenarios.name: part_overlapping_retry_waits_and_part_busy
scenarios.description: A retry of a part that is still being received waits for the first request and then answers duplicate:true. If the first request is still stalled after 5 seconds the retry is 429 part_busy with Retry-After 2. A stalled upload that is abandoned leaves the part unmarked. The 5-second wait is real time.

steps.note: the retry's answer counts the part the original has just marked
a synchronous request for a part another request is still uploading waits the part-lock time, then part_busy

scenarios.name: too_many_parts_in_flight
scenarios.description: At most MaxPartsInFlightPerUser part uploads of one account run at once; one more is 429 too_many_parts_in_flight with Retry-After 1 and is refused before its body is read. Another account is not affected, and the slots are free again as soon as the uploads end.

steps.note: max_parallelism is the account's in-flight cap when that is below 8
another account has its own slots

scenarios.name: upload_interrupted_then_resumed_across_a_restart
scenarios.description: A part whose body is cut off by the client is not marked. After a restart of the server (files.db reopened) the same create returns the same object with the parts already on disk, the parts map says what is missing, complete refuses until it is sent, and the resumed object is whole.

scenarios.name: part_short_body
scenarios.description: A body that ends before Content-Length (here the client half-closes the connection after 1000 bytes and keeps reading) is 400 short_body and the part is not marked; the full part sent again is accepted. A client with an ordinary HTTP stack never sees this answer: it sees its own connection error.

scenarios.name: complete_rules
scenarios.description: complete is 409 incomplete while a part is missing (with the part count and the first 32 missing indices); it is idempotent once the object is whole, and then the object can be read in full. A part sent again to a completed object is a duplicate (same digest) or a conflict (another digest).

scenarios.name: download_range_rules
scenarios.description: One range only: a-b, a- and -n. A whole read is 200; a range is 206 with Content-Range; an end past the size is clipped and a suffix longer than the object is the whole object. A list of ranges, anything unparseable, an empty suffix and a start at or past the end are 416 range_not_satisfiable with Content-Range bytes */size.

scenarios.name: streaming_425_until_the_parts_arrive_and_refusals_spend_nothing
scenarios.description: While an object is still being uploaded, a range over a part that has not arrived is 425 parts_not_yet_received with Retry-After 1 and the first and last part it needs; the header region (bytes 0-63) is always served. Only whole parts on disk are served. A request refused with 425 spends no use of the token and no bytes: the token's two uses are still there after four refusals.

steps.note: the token is issued at creation, before any byte exists
a range that merely touches the missing part is refused too
the owner is refused as well
two uses were spent by the two header reads, none by the refusals

scenarios.name: streaming_prefer_wait_is_answered_when_the_part_arrives
scenarios.description: With Prefer: wait=N the server holds a request for a missing part and answers 206 as soon as the part is on disk; Preference-Applied says how long it was willing to wait.

scenarios.name: streaming_wait_is_capped_and_the_header_region_never_waits
scenarios.description: The wait is capped by the server (here 1 second; 25 by default): asking for more is answered with the capped value in Preference-Applied and, when the part has not arrived by then, 425. wait=0 or an unreadable value means no wait and no Preference-Applied. A range inside the header region never waits and is never marked as applied. The capped wait is real time.

scenarios.name: streaming_delete_wakes_a_waiting_download_with_404
scenarios.description: If the object is deleted while a download waits for its parts, the waiting request gets 404 not_found at once.

scenarios.name: prefer_wait_is_acknowledged_when_the_request_needs_parts_of_an_unfinished_object
scenarios.description: Preference-Applied: wait=N is sent when the request carries Prefer: wait=N and needs parts of an UNFINISHED object, also when those parts turn out to be on disk already (nothing is waited for). It is not sent for the header region, nor for a completed object, nor for a Prefer that carries no wait. The Prefer header may hold several preferences.

steps.note: unfinished, the part is already on disk: acknowledged all the same
the header region needs no part
completed: never acknowledged

scenarios.name: download_check_order_object_authorisation_range_slot_parts
scenarios.description: The checks of a download run in this order, for the owner and for a token holder alike (the owner skips the authorisation): the object exists (404), the caller is authorised (400 bad_token_headers or 403, whatever the Range says: a caller who may not read the object learns nothing about it, not even its size), the Range is satisfiable (416), the account has a free download slot (429), the parts are on disk (425). A request refused on the way spends nothing from its token. The download slots in use are simulated by holding them.

steps.note: an object that does not exist is 404 whoever asks
a stranger with an unsatisfiable range is refused before the range is looked at
a bad token on an unfinished object is 403, not 425
authorisation before the slot
the range before the slot
the slot before the parts (425)
the owner follows the same order

scenarios.name: token_user_scope_defaults_and_bounds
scenarios.description: POST token for one recipient: the answer carries v (64 hex), exp (now + ttl on the server clock), max and scope "user". ttl_seconds defaults to 7 days (at most 30), max_uses to 10 (at most 1000); 0 selects the default. Anything else is 400 bad_token_request, an unknown field or a wrong type 400 bad_request.

scenarios.name: token_binding_tamper_and_expiry
scenarios.description: A user-scope token validates only for the account it was issued for (the account is the authenticated one, not anything the request states). A wrong, tampered, expired or other-object token is 403 token_rejected: the same answer for all, so nothing tells a guesser which part was wrong. Missing claims are 400 bad_token_headers, no token at all 403 token_required. The token is valid up to and including its expiry millisecond. The owner never needs a token.

steps.note: the token of another object
now equals exp: still valid
one millisecond past exp

scenarios.name: token_uses_are_spent_only_by_requests_from_offset_zero
scenarios.description: A use is spent only by a request that starts at offset 0 (the read of the first 64 bytes, or a whole read). Ranged reads that start elsewhere spend none however many there are, and still work after the uses are gone.

steps.note: both uses are spent

scenarios.name: token_byte_cap_is_eight_times_the_blob
scenarios.description: Whatever the number of uses, the bytes served under one token to one account may not pass 8 times the blob length: here eight whole reads are served and the next request, however small, is 403 token_rejected. The owner is not affected.

scenarios.name: token_reissue_starts_a_fresh_budget
scenarios.description: A re-issued token has a new expiry, hence a new value, hence a fresh budget; the old one is not touched and stays spent.

scenarios.name: token_group_scope_membership_is_checked_at_download_time
scenarios.description: A group token is one token for a whole group: any current member can read with it, a non-member is 403 token_rejected (the same answer as a bad token: no membership oracle), each member has a budget of their own, a member removed from the group loses access at once, and a group lookup that fails is a 500 storage_error, never a pass.

steps.note: issued before the upload has started
bob's three uses are spent
carol's budget is her own
removed from the group: refused at once

scenarios.name: token_group_rules_owner_membership_and_scope_limit
scenarios.description: The owner of a group token must be a member of the group (403 not_group_member). A group id must be well formed. An object can be shared with at most 8 groups (409 too_many_group_scopes); issuing again for a group already on the list is not a ninth. A create that asks for a group token the owner may not have is refused whole: nothing is created. A group token can be asked for at creation, and works before the upload.

steps.note: a group already on the list is not a ninth
a member reads the header before any part exists

scenarios.name: tokens_disabled_without_a_secret_only_the_owner_reads
scenarios.description: Without a token secret on the server (503 tokens_disabled) no token can be issued, a create that asks for one is refused before it creates anything, and only the owner can read: any other account is 403 not_owner.

steps.note: obj1 is complete and the refused create made nothing

scenarios.name: group_tokens_unavailable_without_a_group_store
scenarios.description: If the server has no group store, a group token request is 503 groups_unavailable (at create too, which then creates nothing); user-scope tokens are not affected.

scenarios.name: too_many_downloads_spends_no_token_budget
scenarios.description: At most MaxDownloadsPerUser downloads of one account run at once; one more is 429 too_many_downloads with Retry-After 5 and, being refused before the token is charged, spends none of its budget. The slots are per account. The downloads in flight are simulated by holding the slots.

steps.note: the slots are per account
the refusal did not spend the single use

scenarios.name: delete_by_the_owner_frees_the_quota_at_once
scenarios.description: DELETE by the owner, in any state, is 204 and the room is free the moment it answers; every later request for the object is 404 not_found. Another account cannot delete it (403 not_owner). A completed object can be deleted too.

steps.note: the refused delete changed nothing
the quota is free at once
a second delete finds nothing

scenarios.name: object_routes_owner_unknown_object_and_authentication
scenarios.description: Every object route is the owner's: a stranger is 403 not_owner (a read without a token is 403 token_required), an object that does not exist is 404 not_found whoever asks, and a request without authentication is 401 unauthorized.

steps.note: nothing the stranger sent changed the object

scenarios.name: routing_and_methods
scenarios.description: Authentication comes first, then the shape of the path: an object id must be a lowercase UUID (404 otherwise), an unknown sub-route is 404, a method the route does not take is 405 method_not_allowed with an Allow header.

steps.note: authentication comes before routing

scenarios.name: list_unfinished_shape_and_scope
scenarios.description: GET ?state=unfinished lists the caller's own unfinished objects: obj, blob_len, parts, received, created_ms and activity_ms (the server clock; activity is the last part, or the creation). Completed objects and other accounts' objects are never listed; an account with nothing gets an empty array, not null. The order is by object id.

scenarios.name: list_unfinished_paging_with_limit_and_cursor
scenarios.description: limit defaults to 20 (at most 100); next is present only when there are more and is the last object of the page; after=<next> gives the following page; a walk by cursor sees every object exactly once. An after that names no object simply starts after that id.

steps.note: the default page is 20

scenarios.name: collection_routes_refuse_any_other_query
scenarios.description: state=unfinished is mandatory (no request can mean everything); an unknown or repeated parameter, a malformed query string, a limit outside 1..100 or not canonical, an after that is not an object id, and (for DELETE) any parameter but state are all 400 bad_request, and a refused request deletes nothing.

steps.note: nothing was deleted

scenarios.name: delete_unfinished_frees_every_unfinished_object_and_nothing_else
scenarios.description: DELETE ?state=unfinished deletes all the caller's unfinished objects (200 with deleted and freed_bytes, the declared size they held) and frees the quota at once. It never touches a completed object or another account's object, and it is idempotent: with nothing left it answers 200 deleted 0.

steps.note: a partly sent object (its only part) is still unfinished
the completed object is untouched
so is the other account's
the quota was free at once

scenarios.name: cleanup_deletes_an_unfinished_object_six_hours_after_its_last_part
scenarios.description: The cleanup removes an unfinished object once it is MORE than 6 hours past its last part (its creation, if it never got one): at exactly 6 hours it is still there, one millisecond later it is gone. A create after that makes a new object.

steps.note: exactly 6 hours after its creation: kept
6 hours and 1 ms: gone
its last part was 1 hour ago
exactly 6 hours after its last part: kept

scenarios.name: cleanup_deletes_an_unfinished_object_24_hours_after_creation_whatever_its_activity
scenarios.description: A part every 5 hours keeps the 6-hour rule from firing, but an unfinished object is deleted 24 hours after its CREATION whatever it did in between, and nothing a client sends moves that limit (not a part, not a repeated create). At exactly 24 hours it is still there; one millisecond later it is gone and the same create makes a new object.

steps.note: 23 hours after the creation: a repeated create changes nothing
exactly 24 hours: kept

scenarios.name: cleanup_deletes_a_completed_object_30_days_after_completion
scenarios.description: A completed object is kept for its retention (30 days by default, counted from completion; the 6-hour and 24-hour rules are for unfinished objects only). At exactly 30 days it is still there and a token that expires at that same millisecond still works; one millisecond later the object is gone for everybody.

steps.note: 25 hours: the 24-hour rule is not for completed objects

scenarios.name: cleanup_completed_retention_is_configurable
scenarios.description: The retention of a completed object is the server's configuration (14 days in the production configuration): here 14 days, and the object is gone one millisecond after it.

scenarios.name: activity_is_refreshed_only_by_a_new_part
scenarios.description: The idle time that the cleanup measures starts at the last NEW part (the creation, if there has been none). A part sent again (duplicate), a part refused (part_conflict, digest_mismatch, bad_length) and a repeated create do not move it: here they are all made 4 hours in, and the cleanup still deletes the object 6 hours after its last new part, or after its creation, to the millisecond.

steps.note: none of those calls moved activity_ms
6 h and 1 ms after its creation: its repeated create and refused parts did not keep it
5 h after its last new part
exactly 6 h after its last new part, although a duplicate and a refused part came 2 h ago

scenarios.name: stale_objects_count_and_stay_usable_until_the_cleanup_removes_them
scenarios.description: An idle unfinished object keeps counting against the quota and its slot until the cleanup deletes it: waiting past the retention frees nothing, and until the cleanup has actually run the object still takes parts and completes (which also keeps it from being removed). Once the cleanup has removed idle objects their room is free.

steps.note: idle, still counting
6h59m after o1's creation, but no cleanup has run: o1 still holds its slot
the stale object still takes a part (and is thereby active again)
the completion freed a slot
the completed object still counts

scenarios.name: restart_server_preserves_objects_parts_tokens_and_budgets
scenarios.description: After the server restarts (files.db and the blob directory reopened) objects, received parts, issued tokens and the budget already spent under them are all as they were.

steps.note: the token still validates and had one use left
